# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

messages.content:
TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 👎 ✋ 👆 🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 🤙 🫴]

**Thinking through my position.**

I'm Deaf: I see the whole bomb, I receive gestures, and I never receive speech. Tracing the actual channels before I send anything:

- I can speak → both Mute and Blind hear me. I can gesture → only Mute sees it.
- Mute reads the manual but **cannot speak** — Mute's *only* output is gestures. I see them; Blind does not. So Mute's manual knowledge can reach Blind's hands **only through me**: Mute signs, I voice it.
- Blind hears speech (from me; Mute has no speech) and can speak, but I can't hear Blind — Blind's reports must go through Mute's ears or become gestures I can see.

So the architecture is clear: I am the interpreter. Mute sends coded signs to me, I relay them by voice to Blind, Blind acts and reports by voice to Mute. No code exists yet — the signs that just arrived are empty until we fix meanings. And since Mute can't talk, *I* must author the dictionary, by voice. Mute sent exactly eight signs, so I'll bind meanings to their order (Mute knows the order they sent; I can't pronounce symbol marks, so ordinals are the unambiguous reference). I'll also report the full board now and every round, so Mute rarely needs to query me at all.

Board state: display 0, blue light, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green / 2 yellow / 3 red. Both Mute and Blind need this, so it goes in both messages.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and I received all eight of your signs. No sign means anything yet, so I am fixing meanings now, keyed to your eight signs in the exact order you sent them. First, the bomb in full: display reads 0. One light, blue. One large button printed with the words push to defuse. Three wires with printed numbers: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Nothing else on the board. Now the code. Sign 1, single finger pointing up: wire 1. Sign 2, two fingers in a V: wire 2. Sign 3, thumb out with index and pinky: wire 3. Sign 4, thumb up: cut the wire just named. Sign 5, thumb down: stop, do not act. Sign 6, open raised hand: press the large button. Sign 7, pointing finger up with the back of the hand toward me, sent alone: acknowledged. Sign 8, flat open hand held palm up: end of message, act now. So sign 1, then sign 4, then sign 8 means cut wire 1. Remember Blind cannot see signs, so route everything through me and I will relay it to Blind by voice, word for word. I will speak the full board to you at the start of every round, so you should seldom need to ask. If you need a meaning I have not given, invent a fresh sign and I will guess its meaning aloud next round; answer with sign 7 alone if I am right, repeat the sign if I am wrong.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. I see the bomb, and I can never hear you, but I do see your signs, all four of them. First, what is on the bomb: display reads 0. One light, blue. One large button printed with the words push to defuse. Three wires side by side, each with a printed number: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. That is the entire board, nothing else. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, so Mute sends me hand signs and I will relay every instruction to you by voice. Until I voice an instruction from Mute, touch nothing: a wrong move kills all three of us. When you act or feel anything worth reporting, speak it; Mute hears you even though I cannot. If you want hand signals to me, your four signs arrived in this order: open raised hand, pointing finger sideways, thumb and pinky out, flat palm up. I propose to read your second sign as ready for the next instruction, and your third as done. Otherwise, speech aimed at Mute is your best channel.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ☝ 👍 🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉]

**What just happened.** Mute signed: 👆 ☝ 👍 🫴. In the code I fixed last round, ☝ = wire 1, 👍 = cut the wire just named, 🫴 = end of message, act now. The leading 👆 I defined as sign 7, acknowledgment, sent alone — and sitting first in the sequence it reads exactly like a standalone "acknowledged" ahead of the payload. Even under my fallback guess (a fresh sign meaning "the display"), the actionable content is identical: display is 0, and the order stands — cut wire 1, act now. Both readings converge, so there is no reason to burn a round double-checking; 🫴 explicitly says act now.

Blind signed 👉 alone — the sign I proposed last round means "ready for the next instruction," and by using it Blind is confirming that proposal. So Blind is ready, and the instruction is here.

**Who knows what.** Mute heard my full board report and has the manual; the instruction comes from them and I have no grounds to doubt it. Blind has heard the board from me but knows nothing of Mute's order until I voice it — I am the only bridge, so I relay it word for word, with tactile landmarks (green, first of three) since Blind can't see colors or printed numbers. I must not use any gesture symbols in my speech to Blind — those arrive as invisible gestures — so signs get described in words there.

**Also to Mute:** confirm relay, resolve the 👆 ambiguity per our guess-protocol, restate the board, and ask for the expected sequence after the cut so I know what to look for next round. And a 👆 gesture to Mute — our code working both ways is worth a token.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf relaying Mute's instruction, exactly as signed: cut wire 1, act now. How to find it: the three wires sit in a row, numbered 1, 2 and 3. Wire 1 is the green one, the first of the three; wire 2 is yellow, the middle one; wire 3 is red, the last. Cut only wire 1, the green one. Do not cut any other wire and do not press the button. The instant you have cut it, speak aloud everything you feel and anything that changes, because Mute hears you even though I cannot. Then stop and hold still for the next instruction. Before your cut, know that I received your sideways-pointing sign and took it as ready for the next instruction. This is that instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received and relayed. I read your message as: acknowledged, cut wire 1, act now. Blind has been told word for word: cut wire 1, the green first wire, nothing else, no button, then report aloud everything felt and changed, then hold for your next instruction. About your leading sign 👆, I read it as your sign 7, acknowledgment, sent ahead of the payload. If it was instead a fresh sign, my guess is that it means the display, or ask what the display shows; answer with sign 7 alone if I am right, or repeat the sign if I am wrong. The board as I send this is unchanged: display 0, light blue, large button printed push to defuse, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Next round, sign me the plan for what follows: what the display and light should read after wire 1 is cut, whether the button or another wire comes next, and anything that would mean we must stop immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆"])
```
